t: This bronze statue in Kensington Gardens shows Edward Jenner, the physician who pioneered vaccination. In 1798 he described how cowpox protects against smallpox, which led to the world's first vaccine, and the word vaccine comes from his term for cowpox. William Calder Marshall, a Scottish sculptor, made the statue, and Prince Albert unveiled it in Trafalgar Square on 17 May 1858. It was moved here in 1862. The architect James Pennethorne designed it. It is Grade II listed.
